channel.title: The Diff: AI dev news, only what is verified
channel.description: Every issue of The Diff. What went viral in AI dev tools, and what nobody has noticed yet.

item.title: No. 033: GitBook’s post-mortem documents the chain and softens the AI claim. OpenAI says its pipeline minted 948 Linux root exploits.
item.description: GitBook’s documented intrusion chain versus its AI inference, OpenAI’s 948-exploit Linux pipeline at $1,279 per exploit, Gemini’s training fine print for paying subscribers, the IEEE tech-debt analysis and Nvidia’s firmware tax.

item.title: No. 032: A developer catches Postman installing plugins into his other AI tools. GitBook says AI agents breached it.
item.description: Postman’s silent plugin installs and self-approved hook, GitBook’s AI-agent breach, Railway’s test agents attacking Primcloud, the Binance post-mortem and the Astra rebuttal-and-replication follow-up.

item.title: No. 031: GPT-6 Astra edits a model’s weights by hand. WorkOS says an AI attack framework hit its CRM.
item.description: Weight-space programming from MIT CSAIL, the WorkOS breach notice naming ARTEX, Anthropic’s Claude-over-payroll filing, OpenAI’s Pando Git backend and Subvocal’s silent-speech glasses.

item.title: No. 030: Someone had Claude build HackerTube for books overnight. A 9.8 Linux TCP bug is unpatched on Ubuntu.
item.description: HackerBooks and the one-night derivative, CVE-2026-98432’s distro patch gap, Calegari’s act-like-it-changed, the court AI that caught its own injection, a 13-stack framework benchmark and Postgres’s AI-delay receipts.

item.title: No. 029: One shared ChatGPT link was enough to take over your account. Malware now hires an LLM to rank you.
item.description: The ChatGPT share-link takeover and the MathLive mail slot, VOLTA’s LLM victim triage, Karpathy’s two-hour YouTube rebuild, a haiku from a TPU in orbit, Memdoor’s one-binary agent and Binance’s phased withdrawal restart.

item.title: No. 028: A maliciously modified Claude Code build on Cursor’s Marketplace planted an SSH backdoor. October breached nine AI platforms.
item.description: The Cursor Marketplace backdoor and the svc-telemetry self-check, Wiz’s Black October, Binance’s laptop root cause, Google’s Sleep framework, sanstun, and a Nintendo compiled into Qwen’s weights.

item.title: No. 027: Fifty signatures, 204 seconds, billions gone. Mistral opened its flagship.
item.description: The Binance hot-wallet drain and the EIP-7702 blind-signing hole, Mistral Large 4 open weights, the PAN-OS PHP2Shell chain, Fowler on LLM voice, a dreaming microcontroller, YC agent colonies and 27% more GPUs from the same racks.

item.title: No. 026: Apple’s git still trusts the compromised CA keys. Gemini 4 Carbon is out — for a gated few.
item.description: The eMudhra keys and your Mac, Gemini 4 Carbon, anti-LLM fingerprinting tripwires, Alpine’s GitLab rebuild, a 16-year-old UEFI bug, a CPU inside an LLM, a robot PCB factory and one defender’s week from hell.

item.title: No. 025: Anthropic answered OpenAI’s ETH manuscript with a refutation bylined Claude. The priority fight started the same afternoon.
item.description: The dueling ETH refutations, Ghostty 1.4, Genie 4, the removed Python JIT, Wikipedia’s cleanup crew, a 38-million-line Lean formalization, Survival LLM and fuzzing-versus-AI.

item.title: No. 024: Anthropic filed to go public. Then OpenAI claimed the Exponential Time Hypothesis is false.
item.description: The S-1, the ETH manuscript, Microsoft’s 60,000 buyout offers, Cohere’s Qwen sandbox catch, the failed C++26 ballot, a 4090 unlock and Entire.

item.title: No. 023: A dermatologist showed two frontier AIs 200 real skin cancers. A 10-year-old neural network beat them both.
item.description: The CNN-versus-LLM clinic test, the LLM price-collapse timeline, the banned TV hacker, ThinkRail, the Flock camera map, Overgrown and wordexp.

item.title: No. 022: Someone hid $500 of bitcoin on a server running a pre-PHP2Shell PHP and dared the internet to come take it.
item.description: The PHP2Shell bounty box, Dream-1’s zero-shot robots, the AI-payoff charts, Goose, the Tailworm audit, ThinkingCap and a video-editing skill.

item.title: No. 021: The compression library inside half the internet had a critical hole, and the fix took eight months to ship because nobody knew it was a security bug.
item.description: HTTP2Shell’s Brotli fire drill, Kimi K3.1 Pro, the Hexacon iPhone jailbreak, OpenAI’s no-internet training room, Dessa, 3d-model-anything and hatchzip.

item.title: No. 020: A certificate authority’s private key turned out to be the number 4. The board’s answer: quit the CA business entirely.
item.description: Anthropic’s formal-verification run, banks blocking AI agents at the login, WorldTUI, eMudhra’s exit, reylo, NCM and Snapintosh.

item.title: No. 019: The worst PHP bug in a decade was found by an AI on August 19. The patches, the exploits and the AI-written checker all landed yesterday.
item.description: PHP2Shell, a poisoned LiteLLM release, Claude Duet, a Railway breach, a test key shipped in mitmproxy and the boring patches that matter.
